3.0.0.en: The back side of the desert: areas of pasture that follow wide areas of desert.

3.0.1.en: The mountain of God, even to Horeb: Horeb means desert or dry, and Mount Horeb is a range of mountains lying in the south of the Sinai Peninsula. It is called the mountain of God because Moses received the commandments and the Law from its summit. Moses was accustomed to tend the flock of his father-in-law Jethro, and he was eighty years old. One day he led the flock to pasture lands far away in the depths of the desert near Mount Horeb, and he was at that time eighty years old; he had spent forty of them in Pharaoh's palace in Egypt and the next forty in the wilderness of Midian, while the last forty of his life he spent as leader of the people in the wilderness of Sinai until he reached the borders of the land of Canaan; that is, Moses lived 120 years on earth.

3.1.0.en: The bush: a thorny plant that grows in the desert.

3.1.1.en: While Moses was tending the flock, he saw a wonderful sight: a flame of fire surrounding a bramble plant without the plant being burned. He marveled at the sight and turned aside with curiosity to learn the truth of the matter.

3.1.2.en: It says in (v. 2) that the bush burning with fire is an appearance of the angel of the Lord, then it returns in (v. 4) and says that it is the Lord. The word angel means messenger or one sent, and what is meant by the word angel is God sent to us, that is, this is one of the appearances of the Second Hypostasis. Note the repeated appearance of God in the form of fire, as He appeared to Abraham as a burning lamp (Gen 15:17), and after the bush He appeared many times in the form of fire, as in the pillar of fire that led the people in the wilderness (ch. 13:21), and as the fire appeared on the mountain when the commandments and the Law were received (ch. 19:18). The bush burning with fire is a symbol of:

3.1.3.en: (1) The people of God; the thorns signify the evils of the world that surround them, while the fire signifies God, who dwells in the midst of His people and around them to protect them and save them.

3.1.4.en: (2) The Incarnation, that is, the union of divinity with humanity, that is, the fire with the bush.

3.1.5.en: (3) The Virgin, who carried in her womb the fire of divinity: the bush signifies her womb, and Christ is signified by the fire.

3.2.0.en: Moses heard a voice calling him by name; he marveled greatly and answered the voice without knowing who was speaking to him.

3.3.0.en: The voice said to him, put off your shoes, for the ground surrounding the bush is holy ground. The taking off of the shoes signifies the holiness of the place, as we do today when we approach the sanctuary, for the following reasons:

3.3.1.en: 1- The shoe is made of the skins of dead animals, so whoever draws near to God leaves behind the perishing material things, that is, detaches himself from them, in order to be occupied with God.

3.3.2.en: 2- The skins from which the shoes are made signify the skins with which Adam and Eve were clothed, so we take them off in order to put on Christ the Redeemer, who justifies us, because the animal sacrifices were a symbol of Christ, who was sacrificed for us on the Cross.

3.3.3.en: 3- The leather of shoes is what drums are made of, so taking off the shoe means leaving superficial, outward worship and caring for spiritual depth.

3.3.4.en: 4- The kinsman is the nearest person to the dead man, who marries his widow to raise up offspring for the dead man; and if he is not willing to marry her, he takes off his shoe so that the kinsman next to him in relationship may marry her. Taking off the shoe in this case means that this kinsman is not worthy to marry the woman, but the kinsman after him is. So whoever takes off his shoes declares that he is not worthy to be the good shepherd of souls, but that Christ is, and that he is merely a servant to Him.

3.3.5.en: Come forward with reverence when you enter the church, so that you may feel the presence of God, for He is present in it and reveals Himself to the believers in Him who fear Him and reject their evils by repentance in order to meet Him ... He wants to reveal Himself to you and make you feel His presence according to your readiness and your care for Him.

3.4.s.en: (2) The call of Moses to service

3.4.0.en: The One who spoke declared Himself to be God, the God of the fathers of the Hebrew people, so Moses was afraid of the greatness and awesomeness of God and covered his face. This is a declaration that the believers have passed alive to God, and that He even calls Himself their God when He said that He is the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. This is a clear answer to the Sadducees and to everyone who denies the resurrection of the dead and their life after death (Lk 20:27, 28).

3.5.0.en: God showed His fatherhood and His sharing in the suffering of His people in Egypt because of the humiliation they endured from the Egyptians. What is beautiful is that He calls them my people, that is, my own; He declares His fatherhood and His responsibility for them, and despite their many sins He hears their prayers and answers them.

3.6.0.en: I am come down: a figurative expression that shows God's condescension and His care to save His people, His hearing and His answering their prayers.

3.6.1.en: To bring them up: because the land of Canaan is higher in geographical level than the land of Egypt, and the land of Canaan represents freedom, settled life and the worship of God, while Egypt represents slavery and humiliation. That is, to bring them up from humiliation and slavery to a better life.

3.6.2.en: A good land and a large: fertile and big, for it extends from the Mediterranean Sea in the west to the River Euphrates in the east, and from the Taurus Mountains in the north to the Arabian Peninsula in the south.

3.6.3.en: Milk and honey: rich and sweet foods that signify abundant good: the milk from the abundance of pastures and the honey from the abundance of plants.

3.6.4.en: God promises to save His people from the hands of the mighty Egyptians and to bring them out to dwell in the land of Canaan, which is a fertile land whose fertility is expressed by saying that it flows with milk and honey, and He will drive out its inhabitants because of their evils and their abandoning of His worship. God makes clear the names of the peoples whose land He will give to the Jews.

3.6.5.en: It is evident from this that God's condescension to save His people and bring them up is like the condescension of Christ in His Incarnation, by which He saved us from our sins in order to bring us up to heaven.

3.7.0.en: God repeats His sense of the distress of His people, and for this reason He decided to send Moses to lead His people and bring them out of the land of Egypt.

3.7.1.en: Trust in the power of God that is with you, however great or difficult the responsibility may be, because it is God who will work in you to face the powers of the world, and He is stronger than all. So ask for His help, then thank Him for what He has done.

3.8.0.en: Moses failed when he relied on his own strength to save his people, so he fled to the wilderness and lived 40 years in which he felt his weakness before the power of God, the God of heaven, while he was merely a shepherd. Therefore, when God called him from the bush to meet Pharaoh and lead the people, he made excuses because of his weakness.

3.8.1.en: It is good to know your weakness when undertaking the service of God; then He supports you with His grace and you can do all things, because by your humility you let God work freely in you, and you glorify Him.

3.9.0.en: God strengthened Moses by saying "I will be with you", then gave him a sign to strengthen him, namely that they would come out of the land of Egypt and worship God in the wilderness of Sinai, that is, on this very mountain beside the bush.

3.10.0.en: Moses placed a new obstacle in the way of carrying out his mission, namely that he did not know the name of God, the God of the fathers, as peoples know the names of their pagan gods, especially as they were living among many names of gods of the Egyptians; so he asked God about His name, which he would declare to his people.

3.11.0.en: Ehyeh: I am He, or I will be; and the meaning of Ehyeh asher Ehyeh is I will be who I will be.

3.11.1.en: God declared that His name is Ehyeh, that is, I am He, and the meaning of the name is that I am the only God, I am the Existing One, and all other than I is nothing. And He commanded Moses to declare this name of His to the children of Israel.

3.12.s.en: (4) How the children of Israel would come out of Egypt

3.12.0.en: Jehovah: that is, the Existing One whose existence is necessary.

3.12.1.en: God told Moses that the first step in bringing out the children of Israel is to meet their elders, that is, the heads of their tribes and clans, and to declare two things to them:

3.12.2.en: 1- That the name of God is Jehovah Ehyeh, which means, as we said, I am He.

3.12.3.en: 2- That He is the God of their fathers, who promised them many descendants and the inheritance of the land of Canaan, so that they may be assured that He is the God whom they know, who heard their cry and will save them.

3.12.4.en: And He commanded him to tell them of God's concern for them and His hearing of their prayers, and that He would save them from the slavery and humiliation of Egypt, bring them out of it, and settle them in the land of Canaan in the place of its wicked peoples.

3.12.5.en: God hears your prayer and feels your need however long the time may be, and He visits you at the proper time, and He is stronger than all the surrounding circumstances. So be reassured and take courage, because He is with you, and as long as He is with you, you are stronger than all.

3.13.0.en: The second step in bringing out the children of Israel is the entering of Moses and the elders of Israel to meet Pharaoh and declare three matters to him:

3.13.1.en: (1) That the God of the Hebrews has appeared to them.

3.13.2.en: (2) The request for the children of Israel to go out of Egypt and journey three days into the wilderness to offer worship to their God. This was a modest request in which he did not ask Pharaoh for material things, nor that they should depart from Egypt and not return to it; it is merely worship of the God of Israel, as the Egyptians worship their gods. Even so, Pharaoh refused, which shows the hardness of his heart in refusing this modest request.

3.13.3.en: (3) They would offer animal sacrifices to please their God, which signify the sacrifice of Christ. These sacrifices are sacred to the Egyptians, so if the children of Israel slaughtered them before the Egyptians' eyes they would provoke their anger; therefore they asked to go far away to sacrifice to their God. This is a logical request that takes the feelings of the Egyptians into account, and even so Pharaoh refused because of his hardness.

3.14.0.en: God told Moses that Pharaoh would refuse his request, so that Moses would not be disturbed, and He declared to him the third step in bringing them out, which is that God would perform many miracles, namely the ten plagues, that would frighten the Egyptians so that they would be compelled to obey God and let His people go.

3.15.0.en: Her that sojourneth in her house: that is, the woman who lodges with her.

3.15.1.en: You shall put them upon your sons, and upon your daughters: that is, your sons and your daughters shall wear them, and the males in this age sometimes wore gold and silver.

3.15.2.en: He commanded him that when they went out of Egypt they should ask the Egyptians for gold, silver and clothing, and God would give them favor in their eyes so that they would give them much, because of their fear of their God who struck them with the ten plagues. In this way God returns to the children of Israel something of their rights that the Egyptians had taken away by enslaving them and putting them to forced labor.

3.15.3.en: This command is not theft, because it is God who commands it. It is a symbol of the spiritual person who believes in God: when God accepts his repentance and saves him from his sins, He gives him many spoils, which are his abilities and gifts that were enslaved to sin, so he is set free and lives with them with God.

3.15.4.en: The continuation of the dialogue with God

4.0.s.en: (1) The miracles of God given to Moses

4.0.0.en: Moses expected that the elders of his people would not believe him, so he asked God what he should do.

4.1.0.en: God asked him what was in his hand, and he said it was a rod. This was not because God did not know, but so that Moses would be certain that it was a rod, so that the miracle would appear afterward by its turning into a serpent.

4.2.0.en: God commanded Moses to cast the rod on the ground, and it became a serpent, so Moses was afraid and ran away from it, for the Holy Bible to confirm that it was a real serpent, so that the turning of the rod into a serpent was a clear miracle.

4.3.0.en: Moses obeyed God and took hold of the serpent by its tail, and it became a rod in his hand. The turning of the serpent into a rod declares:

4.3.1.en: 1- The authority of God over nature and all creatures, so that He changes each of them into the other.

4.3.2.en: 2- The authority of the believer over Satan, who is signified by the serpent, and over the various animals and creatures by the power of God.

4.4.0.en: By this sign the elders of Israel will believe that the God of the fathers has appeared to Moses, and in this He answered his question and his perplexity that he mentioned in (v. 1). This is the first miracle.

4.5.0.en: The second miracle is that Moses put his hand inside his garment and then took it out, and it was leprous, that is, shining white like snow, and then he put it back inside his garment, and it returned as it was, like the rest of the color of his body. This miracle shows God's ability to bring sickness and to heal from it, especially the disease of leprosy, from which none but God can heal.

4.6.0.en: God gave him a third miracle, which was to take some water from the river and pour it on the ground, and it would become blood. This signifies the blood of Christ the Redeemer, which changes our hearts, weak as water, into life, whose symbol is blood. These three miracles prove to the children of Israel that Moses has met God, and they are also a confirmation of Moses' faith.

4.6.1.en: God gives you grace in the eyes of people so that they may know that you are with God. So do not care about the opinion of people, because God will give you grace in their eyes, but only obey Him and declare His voice.

4.7.0.en: Neither heretofore, nor since: that is, throughout his past life.

4.7.1.en: Nor since thou hast spoken unto thy servant: since God appeared to Moses in the bush.

4.7.2.en: Moses' humility is shown in his excuse for not leading the people, and his argument is his weakness in speech throughout his life; he may have had some difficulty in pronouncing certain letters, being, for example, a lisper. His feeling now is entirely different from his feeling when he left the palace 40 years ago to save his people, when he was relying on his own strength; now he feels his weakness and declares it before God.

4.7.3.en: Declare your weakness before God before any work or any service or speech, and you will receive grace and strength from Him to succeed in everything, and even to be distinguished from those around you, and God will be glorified in you.

4.8.0.en: God reassured Moses that He is the Creator of man and of the tongue, and likewise He permits any incapacity in human beings and is also able to complete it. Therefore He is able to complete Moses and support him in his mission however great his weakness or incapacity.

4.9.0.en: Because of Moses' strong sense of his weakness, he repeated his excuse and asked God to send another in his place. This was a mistaken exaggeration on Moses' part; he ought to have obeyed God since He had reassured him.

4.9.1.en: Do not make excuses for any service that God places before you, and trust in His power that supports you after you have revealed your weakness to God.

4.10.0.en: Despite Moses' mistake, God accepted his excuse and strengthened him with a person who would be with him and speak as an official spokesman in his name, namely his brother Aaron, who would go out, by God's guidance, to meet Moses when he returned from Midian to Egypt, and would rejoice at meeting him. But he would be merely a spokesman for Moses, while Moses would be the leader and head over him. Then He reminded him to take the rod with him, with which he would perform the miracles. Aaron later caused problems for Moses by making the golden calf when Moses went up to receive the tablets of the Law on the mountain; would that he had listened to God's word and obeyed and trusted in Him and had not persisted in his excuse.

4.10.1.en: Note that God reminded him to take the rod, which is a small tool, but with it God would perform great miracles, so that the glory would be to God and not to the tool, just as God uses weak people to be glorified in them, namely His prophets and His messengers, and as He also uses simple natural materials such as water and oil for the Holy Spirit to dwell in them and give the Holy Sacraments to those who believe in Him in the Church.

4.10.2.en: Do not be stubborn with God, but obey Him quickly so as not to cause problems for yourself.

4.11.0.en: Moses asked leave of his father-in-law Jethro to return and save his people in Egypt, and he gave him leave. Of course this means that he took his wife and his sons with him.

4.12.0.en: Here the reason for Moses' strength in his decision to return to Egypt is shown: God had already reassured him that Pharaoh and his counselors who had wanted to kill him long ago were dead, and He commanded him to go to the elders of Israel and then to the new Pharaoh.

4.13.0.en: Moses set out with his wife and his sons, and they rode on donkeys, and he took with him his rod, which God had commanded him to take with him in order to perform many miracles with it, and then he traveled to Egypt. This rod is a symbol of the wood of the Cross.

4.14.0.en: God commanded Moses to perform the three miracles with the elders of Israel so that they would believe that it was God who had sent him to them, and then to perform them also before Pharaoh to convince him of the power of God that was with him. And God warned Moses that Pharaoh would harden his heart and refuse to believe in God and submit to Moses, so he should not be disturbed by this refusal. Note that God does not harden anyone's heart toward evil, but He leaves a person to his evil if he insists on it.

4.14.1.en: When God warns us that there are afflictions on the way of the Kingdom, He wants us not to be disturbed by them when we meet them and to trust in His power that supports us; indeed, out of His love He turns them to our good so that they become steps for us that raise us up to heaven.

4.15.0.en: God told Moses the end of the dialogue that would take place between him and Pharaoh after he had struck him with nine plagues, namely His saying to him in the end that God commands you to let the people of Israel go, my firstborn son, because it is the only people that believes in Him at that time, while the rest of the peoples, his brothers, will believe later at the Incarnation of Christ. And because Pharaoh would be stubborn in releasing the Israelite people, the firstborn son of God, God would kill his firstborn together with the firstborn of all the Egyptians, and this is what happened in the tenth plague, so Pharaoh submitted and let the people go.

4.15.1.en: Do not resist God by rejecting His commandments, lest He punish you, and if He punishes you, repent quickly and He will forgive you and you will find your place in eternity.

4.16.0.en: While Moses was traveling, he rested on the way at a lodging place prepared on the road like an inn, called the inn. There God appeared to him and rebuked him for neglecting to circumcise his son; perhaps in this he had been led by the feelings of his wife Zipporah in her fear and pity for the child. In order that God might show him the seriousness of neglecting obedience to His commands, He attacked him to kill him, perhaps in the form of an angel; and this threat was also to frighten Zipporah, that her neglect could lead to the death of her husband, especially since God had been long-suffering toward Moses, for He appeared to him in the bush and spoke with him in the wilderness and in Midian and charged him with leading the people, and all these were opportunities for him to pay attention to obeying God and to circumcise his son.

4.16.1.en: Do not be careless in obeying God's commandments, relying on His love and long-suffering, because if He is perfect in His tenderness, He is also perfect in His justice, and by your disobedience you expose yourself to destruction. Let the fear of God be always before your eyes, and you will live in assurance and be made fit to know God and enjoy fellowship with Him.

4.17.0.en: A sharp stone: a serrated piece of flint used as a knife.

4.17.1.en: Zipporah remembered her sin in preventing her husband from circumcising his son, out of her fear for him from this surgical operation, and she had not believed in the importance of obeying God's commandment; but when she saw her husband exposed to death she hurried to correct her mistake by performing the circumcision on her son. Then she took the piece of skin stained with blood and touched Moses' feet, her husband's, with it, and said to him "a bloody husband art thou to me", that is, I believe that I am married to you and I circumcise my children, and I believe that the blood saves me from every sin as you taught me; for she declares that by circumcising her son she regained Moses, who was about to die at the hand of the angel, as a husband and bridegroom to her, and regained him by the blood shed through circumcision, which signifies the blood of Christ.

4.18.0.en: The angel left Moses after the circumcision was completed, and Zipporah confirmed her words that Moses was a bloody husband to her, that is, that her marriage and her family depend on the blood shed in circumcision, which signifies the blood of Christ the Redeemer.

4.19.0.en: God informed Aaron that Moses was returning to Egypt and commanded him to meet him, so he went out to him and kissed him and rejoiced at meeting him after 40 years of separation.

4.20.0.en: Moses told Aaron of his meeting with God, who appeared to him in the bush, and of all the conversation that took place between them and the miracles that He gave him to perform in order to bring his people out of Egypt.

4.21.0.en: Moses and Aaron gathered the elders of Israel, and Aaron, as spokesman for Moses, told them of God's appearance to his brother and the conversation that took place between them, and then Moses performed the miracles before them to confirm God's appearance to him.

4.22.0.en: The elders of Israel rejoiced and worshiped God, declaring their faith in Him and their submission to Moses. Of course the news spread among the people of Israel, and they rejoiced that God had answered their prayers.

4.22.1.en: Trust that God hears your prayers with care, and if He delays in answering, it is in order to increase your faith and save you from many sins and show His care for you at the proper time. So persevere in your prayers however long the time, confident of His love, and be faithful in your spiritual striving and in fulfilling your duties, for He will never leave you. The Book of Genesis. The meeting with Pharaoh and his punishing of the children of Israel
